title: Does Turmeric Really Heal? The Liverdoc Explains
description:
Turmeric (Haldi) is often called the king of Indian spices. From curries to haldi doodh, it is believed to cure cough, cold, pain, digestive problems, and even serious illnesses. But does turmeric really work as medicine, or is it just a cultural myth?

In this video, Dr. Abby Philips (The Liver Doc) — a liver specialist and global expert on herb-induced liver injuries (HILI) — explains what the science says about turmeric and curcumin supplements. We discuss:

Why a pinch of turmeric in food has no real medicinal effect.
What randomized control trials reveal about turmeric’s claims.
Why curcumin supplements are popular but not backed by strong clinical evidence.
What international medical bodies say about turmeric use.
The hostility Dr. Abby faced when he shared scientific truths about turmeric.
The possible side effects and liver risks of excess curcumin.
Why anecdotes (“turmeric cured me”) aren’t evidence.

If you’ve searched for “turmeric science,” “curcumin supplement safety,” “haldi doodh myth,” “turmeric liver damage,” or “Dr Abby Liver Doc turmeric”, this video gives you the rational perspective. Don’t forget to subscribe, like, comment, and share…

Host: Dr Abby Philips M.D., D.M (Clinical Scientist, Hepatology) at Rajagiri Hospital, Aluva, Cochin, Kerala, India
